A1.justification: Both PDFs describe A Machine-Learned Comorbidity Index and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIMIC-III/IV model evaluations, theory diagnostics, encoder/kernel ablations, and empirical risk curves in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original MIMIC-III/IV experiments, ablations, and risk curves, and reports revised numerical diagnostics.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.6 revise the stated Stage-1 checkpoint selection and task-weight calibration from task-specific validation nHSIC to validation nHSIC against a common in-hospital mortality anchor. The encoder and weighted multi-outcome objective remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the underlying experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV ICD-10 cohorts on in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, prolonged stay, and ICU transfer. The dataset-specific ICU definitions and appendix task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and 6–7 retain the same clinical, classical, and neural comparator sets. The new clinical-index subsection documents existing CCI, ECI, and CCI+ECI baselines; removing the Liu citation does not remove the DeepSets comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 changes the stated Stage-1 checkpoint-selection criterion to mortality-anchored validation. Section 8 also now describes its objective diagnostics using floored normalization. Patient splits, training budgets, benchmark metrics, and diagnostic cohort sizes remain unchanged; newly disclosed sampling and estimator settings do not establish additional protocol changes.

E4.justification: Section 8 revises the evidence testing whether the shared direction captures multi-outcome structure and selects the full-objective threshold, particularly for MIMIC-III in Tables 3–5. Appendix C's encoder/kernel ablations and Appendix E's risk-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendices A.5 and A.11 newly specify seed 12345 for bandwidth sampling and MI estimation, with deterministic offsets for validation/test nHSIC. Neural results still use seeds 11, 101, and 1001 with mean±SD reporting; no additional repetitions or uncertainty procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces MIMIC-III's matching splits (11265, 11265) with (6707, 11128), changes the selected tail from 5.40% to 6.56%, and changes its certificate from 0.220 to 0.175. This reverses an important diagnostic finding. Tables 3 and 5 also revise MIMIC-III diagnostics. Smaller traditional-index updates occur in Tables 1–2 and 6–7, including CCI mortality MI from 0.01635 to 0.01597 nats. MLCI benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 6.3 and Appendix B replace the uniform additive approximation bound and near-optimality corollary with a rank-one retention theorem defining gamma and proving a multiplicative comparison guarantee. Appendix B also adds canonical threshold levels and a floor-size condition preserving threshold certificates. The noise-averaging lemma is retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: nonlinear multi-outcome learning of one comorbidity score, shared-ordering and threshold theory, and strong dependence results on MIMIC-III/IV. Revised diagnostics qualify supporting interpretations without redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: Section 8 now limits observed threshold agreement to MIMIC-IV and attributes MIMIC-III's divergence to its more balanced length-of-stay endpoint and residual task-specific variation. It also interprets objective ratios through rank-one retention. The limitations section and appendix clinical-use qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and project-page links, hardware information, initialization and sampling details for fixed bandwidth estimation, the 20,000-admission caps, MI's five-neighbor setting, and preprocessing/aggregation instructions for existing clinical-index baselines. These improve documentation; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: v2 removes Liu et al. (2020) from the related-work discussion, baseline citation, and bibliography. The broader positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged. The revised Zaheer reference identifies the same previously cited Deep Sets work.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and explanatory revisions, rewritten theory and diagnostic passages, and a new clinical-index subsection with subsequent appendix renumbering. The overall main-text narrative and Appendices A–E structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 3's headers and caption now identify floored objectives, and Appendix B's notation table changes its entries. Front-page resource links and local text reflow alter layout. All five numbered figures are retained, including identical appendix risk-curve graphics.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through concrete implementation and access information, and Section 8 explicitly acknowledges the MIMIC-III threshold disagreement previously reported as agreement. Appendix B adds a useful condition connecting floored objectives to threshold certificates. The score-dependent retention guarantee replaces the earlier explicit uniform error bound, making the theoretical revision a tradeoff. Overall, the clearer documentation and more qualified empirical interpretation support a modest quality improvement.
